John, the author of Revelation, describes a mighty angel descending from heaven holding a key to the bottomless pit and a great chain. The binding of Satan represents the ultimate defeat of evil and the establishment of God's kingdom. The Lake of Fire often described as a place of eternal torment symbolizes the ultimate consequence of sin and rebellion against God. It represents the eternal loss of fellowship with God and the eternal suffering that results from this separation. This is a sobering reminder of the importance of choosing to follow Christ. It emphasizes the gravity of our decisions and the eternal consequences that await those who reject God's offer of salvation. It is important to remember that God desires all to come to repentance and receive his gift of eternal life. The Lake of Fire is not a place God wants anyone to go, but it is the ultimate consequence of choosing to live apart from Him. Section 7. The New Heaven and the New Earth. A promise of eternity. This new creation is a place of eternal joy and fellowship with God, where His presence dwells forever. The New Heaven and New Earth represent the ultimate fulfillment of God's promise to His people. Here are two things that you need to know about the mainstream media. One, the news is a multi-billion dollar industry. Two, the media companies choose a handful of stories to cover each and every single day. That means that there's a 24 hour slot that needs to be filled with content. And guess what? The narrative is controlled in order to create a reaction in you, a reaction of fear, a reaction of doubt, a reaction of uncertainty, the reason for this is simple. In the media's eyes, your fear equals money. There are so many great things happening in the world right now that we do not hear about through the mainstream media. We don't hear about people's wins. We don't hear about their breakthroughs. We don't hear about the really powerful, positive, good changes which are happening. We're living in such an abundant time, yet most people don't realize that because of the programming that they're led to believe. Humans have an innate instinct to keep each other informed. This is not going to change any time soon. Obsession for searching for the truth has helped us in the long run. But good intentions can always be exploited through organizations and corporations who understand human psychology and have their own agendas at play. I need you to take back your power. This is Regan Hillier and thank you so much for watching. Over 7 billion people are being controlled and manipulated right now. Please take a stand, share this video, and let yourself and the whole world know that you are not willing to be controlled, programmed or manipulated, and you're not willing to let your loved ones be controlled either. Transcript: Tracking a mission's historic return to Earth, a year of science on board the space station, and the safe arrival of the station's newest resident astronaut, a few of the stories to tell you about this week at NASA. The return to Earth of OSIRIS-REX, our first ever asteroid sample return mission is nearly complete. On September 24th, as the O-REX spacecraft approaches Earth, it will release a capsule containing about 8.8 ounces of sample material collected from asteroid Bennu. Following a parachute-assisted landing in the Utah desert, the capsule will be retrieved and eventually shipped to our Johnson Space Center for examination in a pristine curation facility. Transcript: Did you know that certain types of tree bark are edible? This knowledge could come in handy if you should find yourself in a survival situation. Stay tuned to learn more about tree cambium. During the spring and summer months, there are many wild edibles that one can choose from. When late autumn rolls around, the options begin to dwindle. And by the time winter hits, wild food sources become scarce. But even in the winter time nature provides an emergency food cache for those who really need it. To find these emergency caches, one doesn't need to look any further than the trees that surround them. This emergency food lays underneath the outer layer of bark in certain species of trees. Between the outer layer of bark and the actual wood of the tree is a thin layer of inner bark called cambium. The cambium layer is only a couple of millimeters thick. But it is packed with digestible starches, vitamins, minerals, and a little bit of sugar. Cambium also contains a large amount of fiber. Now though all trees have cambium, not all cambium is edible. That's because some trees are known to be toxic for human consumption. Here are some species of trees that are generally safe to gather cambium from. Birch, willow, maple, spruce, pine, and fur. There are other trees out there that contain edible cambium, but those are the main ones. However, all the mentioned species of trees have multiple subspecies. For example, there are literally dozens of different kinds of pine. And so although most species of pine are edible, not all of them are. This is why it is extremely important that you thoroughly research the trees in your area to discover which ones are toxic for human consumption and which ones are good to gather from. Traditionally, pine is the most popular choice when it comes to harvesting cambium. Personally, pine is the only species that I've harvested cambium from, and I've only eaten cambium a few times in my life. Like I said before, cambium is classified as an emergency food. That's because removing the cambium layer will stun the tree's growth at best and can easily kill it at worst. The cambium is where the tree's nutrients are transported up from the roots and into the leaves. And so without the cambium, the tree will quickly starve. Since trees are such a slow growing and valuable resource, the cambium should not be harvested under normal circumstances. It is just not worth harming or possibly killing a tree for a simple snack. So here are the only two circumstances that one should harvest cambium under. Number one, if a person finds themselves in a survival situation and they need something to eat. Number two, if the tree is already being harvested for firewood or lumber. Today I will be harvesting some pine cambium, and although I'm not in a survival situation, I will be returning to harvest this pine tree in the near future. I used my axe to carefully shave away the outer layer of bark, being very careful not to accidentally remove the delicate cambium layer. In a survival situation, it is better to remove small patches like this from several trees rather than harvesting all the way around a single tree. A tree can recover from having a small patch of cambium removed, but it will die from having its cambium removed from all the way around. However, in a survival situation, it's best to harvest whatever is available. Human life takes precedence over trees. In the case that the tree will be harvested for materials anyway, you might as well harvest as much cambium as you possibly can from it. Now that the cambium layer is exposed, all I have to do is gently shave it from the tree. Cambium feels soft and a little gummy. It is also very easy to bend, and it is very easy to peel away from the tree after starting a cut. It might be hard to see in the video, but the wood of the tree is slightly more yellow and color than the whitish looking cambium. It's pretty easy to tell the difference between the two layers since cambium is easy to peel away, but the wood itself will barely peel at all. In a survival situation, probably the best way to eat cambium is straight from the tree. From my experience, I find that pine cambium can vary slightly and taste in texture. Sometimes it's mild and flavor and easy to eat. Other times it can taste quite bitter and is a little harder to chew. I've noticed that cambium gathered in the dead of winter is likely to be the most pleasant and easy to eat, but since I haven't eaten much cambium myself, I can't confirm if that's generally the case for all cambium. But whether it tastes good or not, cambium contains a good amount of nutrients to keep you going if need be. You may want to chew the cambium to extract the nutrients and spit it out, or you may want to swallow the cambium to have something in your stomach. There are pros and cons for each, but if you want to cook the cambium, you can make a sort of tree pasta by tearing the cambium into strips so that they loosely resemble noodles and boil them. Boiling the cambium will make it easier to eat and a little more palatable to taste. When you're done eating your tree pasta, make sure to drink the water that they were boiled in as well. Pine cambium has also been collected, dried, and ground into flour. In countries like Sweden and Finland, this pine flour has been used to make pine bark bread for centuries. Today however, I'll be frying my cambium strips in olive oil with salt until they turn brown and crunchy. I call them cambium chips, and they don't taste all that bad, but I'll give you a fair warning. Hot oil, especially over an open flame, can easily ignite. This would obviously destroy your precious batch of cambium in a heartbeat. Believe me, this has happened to me before, so be very careful. If you feel the pan is getting too hot, or if you see the oil smoking, you'll probably only have seconds to remove it from the flames before ignites. The cambium chips definitely have a pine flavor to them, but if the batch of cambium is a mild one, the flavor mixes quite well with an oil and salt. It's an acquired taste for some, but I really like it.

Transcript: Welcome to today's devotional, focusing on Ephesians 6 for 17. Title the helmet of salvation, protecting your mind from falsehood. Scripture focus. And take the helmet of salvation, Ephesians 6, 17. As we explore the armor of God described by the Apostle Paul, we come to the helmet of salvation. Like every other piece, this is not merely symbolic. It plays a crucial role in guarding one of the most important battlegrounds of our spiritual lives. Paul writes in Ephesians 6 for 17, and take the helmet of salvation. Just as a physical helmet shields a soldier from deadly blows, the helmet of salvation protects our minds from spiritual assaults that aim to weaken our faith and erode our confidence in Christ. This isn't a passive piece of armor. It's an active defense we must intentionally put on every day. In ancient warfare, helmets were more than just protective gear. We bore insignias that identified a soldier's allegiance. For example, a Roman soldier's helmet often displayed designs showing that he belonged to Caesar's army. Similarly, the helmet of salvation marks us as God's own. It declares that through Jesus Christ, we are secure, protected by His grace, and identified as His children. But what happens when we neglect this spiritual helmet? When we let doubt creep in, or forget to equip ourselves daily, we become vulnerable to the enemy's attacks. The enemy loves to target the mind, where fear, confusion, and insecurity can take root. Without our helmet, these attacks can distort our understanding of who we are in Christ. Yet salvation is not a fleeting moment. It's a continuous process of renewal. It constantly reminds us that we are not defined by past failures or sins, but by our relationship with God. When doubts arise, or when the enemy whispers lies about our worth or identity, it is the helmet of salvation that shields our mind, reminding us of the truth. We are beloved, chosen, and secure in Christ. The mind is where some of the fiercest spiritual battles are fought. The enemy knows that a mind fixed on God is powerful, so he aims to cloud our thoughts with lies and distortions of reality. Just as Satan twisted God's words to deceive Eve, he tries to confuse us today. He whispers accusations of inadequacy, plants seeds of self-doubt, and cultivates fear. How often have you found your mind spiraling into anxious thoughts or feelings of unworthiness? Wearing the helmet of salvation means guarding our thoughts with the truth of God's word. Romans 12, verse 2, urges us to be transformed by the renewing of your mind. This renewal isn't a one-time event, it's a daily process. By filling our minds with the promises of God and rejecting the enemy's lies, we actively defend ourselves. We remind ourselves of the salvation we have in Christ and silence anything that contradicts his love and grace. Consider David before his battle with Goliath. When King Saul offered him armor, David declined, knowing it wasn't right for him. Instead, David put his trust in God, not in man-made protection, 1 Samuel 17, 38-39. His confidence in God became his mental armor, guarding him against fear and doubt. Likewise, when we wear the helmet of salvation, we stand firm in the face of spiritual attacks. Our confidence is not in our own strength, but in Christ's saving work, which protects our minds from the enemy's attempts to destabilize us. Like David, we can trust that our salvation in God is our ultimate defense, no matter the size of the giants we face. The helmet of salvation is more than a symbol. It's a necessity we must wear daily. As we navigate the battlefield of the mind, it's crucial to guard our thoughts, renew our minds, and root our confidence in Christ's saving work. Wearing this helmet protects us from the enemy's lies and keeps us grounded in the truth of who we are in Christ. When doubt, fear, or insecurity strike, remember that your salvation is certain. David facing Goliath, you stand firm not because of your own strength, but because of the unshakable security you have in God. The helmet of salvation doesn't just protect your mind, it secures your very identity as a child of God. So wear it daily with confidence, knowing that in Christ your victory is assured. Prayer for today, O Lord our God, thou art the strength and shield of thy people. We thank thee for the helmet of salvation, that guards our minds and protects our hearts from the enemy's deceptions. Help us to wear this helmet daily, standing firm in the assurance of thy saving grace. When doubt and fear assail us may thy truth be our defense, and may we cling to the promise that we are thine, secured for ever in thy hands. We renew our minds, that we might set our thoughts on things above and grant us the wisdom to reject the lies of the adversary. Lead us O shepherd of our souls and protect us with thy mighty hand. In the name of thy son our Savior we pray. Next time in the armor of God's series we explore the sword of the spirit. Let's continue standing firm together in the face of evil. Thank you for joining today's devotional brought to you by sacred thoughts.

Okay, for our next experiment, we're going to make a balloon and flake without blowing it up. You'll need a balloon, a bottle, baking soda, and vinegar. Look, the balloon inflates all by itself. That's because the mixture creates a gas called carbon dioxide, which fills up the balloon. Remember kids, science is all around us, and it's super fun to explore. These experiments show us just how amazing and surprising our world can be. Transcript: The Lives of the Saints by Father Alben Butler, October 24, St. Martin of Virtue. We know practically nothing certain about the saint since the two surviving biographies were written several centuries after his death and narrate mainly his miracles. Moreover, St. Martin of Braga, who was bishop of Dhumium in Portugal, has been confused with St. Martin of Virtue, who lived as a hermit in the forest of Dhumin in Brittany. Our saint was born in Nantes, in the bosom of a Frankish family. St. Felix conferred on him the Diaconate and sent him to preach in Poit-2. According to legend, in spite of all his efforts, Martin only succeeded in converting the owners of the house in which he lived. He advised them to flee from the approaching catastrophe, and he himself left the city where he had worked in vain. Immediately after his departure, an earthquake destroyed it, and it was covered by the waters. The site is now called Lake Grand Lue, and the town of Herboja, on the shore of the lake, replaces the one that was submerged. In addition, there is a men here, or stone column, nearby. Since the wife of the owner of the house where St. Martin lived, turned her eyes towards the city and was converted into a statue. About this legend, we can repeat the moderate comment that Camden makes about a similar fable that is told about Lynn Safadin, of Brekenshire. I suspect that it is a simple fable, and as such, it must be considered. After his missionary failure, St. Martin withdrew to a forest on the left bank of the Seyivra, where he founded a hermitage that became in time the Abbey of Ver2. The saint evangelized the region. Several other foundations are attributed to him, such as that of the Convent of the Nons of Duryu, where he died. It is said that the monks of Ver2 stole the body of their master while the nuns of Duryu were singing the evening office of the dead on the eve of the burial. Among other legends told about St. Martin of Ver2, who is confused in this case with his namesake of Braga. It is said that an English prince had a daughter possessed by evil spirits. One of the demons declared, through the mouth of the young girl, that he could only be vanquished by the prayers of a holy man named Martin. Immediately, the prince sent messengers in all directions in search of the man of God. Finally, the messengers arrived in Ver2 and convinced St. Martin to accompany them. No sooner had the saint set foot in England than the demon sensed his approach and not wanting to face him, he tormented his victim for the last time and fled. It's difficult to love somebody who doesn't return that love or seems undeserving of it. Yes, there is an element of joy and happiness that results from selfless giving with no expectations of anything in return. Sometimes it can be difficult to remain detached when someone is taking advantage or abusing your goodwill. But in general, giving without attaching any strings can bring joy and happiness to both yourself and the receiver. You have to remain detached and not attach any strings to your giving or giving too much, otherwise your risk being taken advantage of. Putting a balance between giving and not expecting anything in return, it can be beneficial, provided one must remain detached and do not develop unhealthy attachments. Like for example, like developing a codependent relationship in which one party is overly emotionally invested or becoming overly attached. It's important to maintain balance and all things. Detachment simply means not expecting anything in return. It doesn't mean not caring or having zero empathy. It just means not attaching any strings to your giving. It is possible to feel empathy or compassion for someone without being overly emotionally invested and without having expectations of anything in return. Detachment is more of an attitude of not expecting anything but still being engaged and involved in the world and other lives. It's giving with no expectations of anything in return. It's giving for the sake of giving without expecting anything or hoping for anything in return. It is a selfless act, one that is purely motivated by wanting to help somebody else. It means not expecting anything from the other person, not expecting repayments or gratitude or any type of response. It's a form of giving that is free from any strings or conditions. By practicing detachment, you are freeing yourself from attachment and desire. And I understand that it helps bring you closer to truth, closer to enlightenment which ultimately helps to bring liberation from the chains of karma and suffering. In general, all selfless acts that are done with true compassion and good intention can help reduce karma. Giving in a detached way is a wonderful example of this. Yeah, I know. More people are opening their emails on their mobile devices and your email must be optimized for all devices. Fifth, include a clear call to action. Emails without a clear call to action won't drive results. Your CTA must be visible, relevant, and easy to follow. Lastly, track and analyze your results. You need to know which emails were opened, clicked, and converted into sales. This data will help you refine and improve future email campaign. In conclusion, the key to successful email marketing is personalization, relevance, and value. If you follow the tips outlined here, you'll be well on your way to creating a killer email marketing campaign in 2023. Thanks for watching, and don't forget to subscribe, like this video, and share it with your friends for more marketing tips and tricks. If you want to learn more about email marketing, click on the link in the description.

The Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering, but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. So Cain was very angry and his face was downcast. Then the Lord said to Cain, Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast? If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door. It desires to have you, but you must rule over it. Now Cain said to his brother Abel, Let's go out to the field. Now they were in the field Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him. Today you are driving me from the land and I will be hidden from your presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth and whoever finds me will kill me. But the Lord said to him, Not so. Everyone who kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over. Then the Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one who found him would kill. So Cain went out from the Lord's presence and lived in the land of Nod, instead eating. Adam made love to his wife again and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, saying, God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him. Seth also had a son and he named him Enoch. At that time people began to call on the name of the Lord. Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Transcript: Hi everyone, it's Ms. Dragonfly, the relationship whisperer back again. Now today's topic is, should you get back with your ex? Now, it's safe to say that everyone has an ex. And for whatever reason, you could not get along together in the first place, and so you split up. The break could have come as an abrupt clean break, with neither of you meeting up ever again, or stretched over a period of time, with little meetings stretching the break up on until you both agree this is going to be the final meeting. However, either way, a physical break up does not mean that you've gotten over your ex, and it is quite common for people not to have gotten over their ex for quite some time. During this time, you might think about your ex, feel like contacting them again to meet up, or even ask them to be... To be friends! With you? Simply because you don't want to let go entirely, and hope to hang on to something with them. They may or may not accept your proposal to be friends with you. If they do accept, then you would both be continuing to drag out your relationship, along with no real ending. If the relationship was painful before, then you're just going to be continuing the pain, and dragging it on. If they say no. To remaining friends with you, then because it was you that wanted to maintain a connection with them, then you're going to feel rejected, and feel additional hurt. Once you no longer have contact with them, then later you will feel lonely, then think about all the good times you had with your ex, and then thinking about getting back with them. You were either consciously forget about the reason why you broke up in the first place, or reason that it's going to be different this time, because you have now developed ways to handle the situation, and not let it get out of hand again, like it did last time. So should you get back with your ex? Well think about the following. You obviously broke up with your ex because of a big issue that you both could not resolve. Many people are willing to overlook and ignore small issues, so you had obviously broke up over big issues. Next, has anything changed now? Let's think about it. More importantly, has that big issue and big difference that caused the breakup gone away? If not then, the issue is still there, and it will be the same story again and end up with the same result. Usually it is a fundamental difference in your human nature that is the problem, like different goals or values that would be significant enough to cause a breakup. So I would say, do not get back with your ex, no matter how tempting it is and how lonely you are now. Even if your ex agreed to get back, nothing would have changed even though you would both be making an effort again at the restart. Basically, you will be back into the same situation, you were as those differences were fundamental enough to have caused the breakup in the first place. And those differences were fundamental to your human nature, to both your human nature. Also, by trying to cling onto a relationship with someone that isn't really compatible with you, you are wasting time that could be better spent finding a partner that is truly compatible with you. You will basically be missing out on opportunities and meeting better partners, therefore it's best not to get back with your ex. Assign them to your dating history and learn from that experience instead, and they are now another type you should avoid. So those are my thoughts. What do you think? Let me know by leaving your comments below and if you've enjoyed the video then don't forget to like, share and subscribe. And for more info on relationships, check out this video. Well that's it for this segment and until I see you next, remember to stay safe, confident and gorgeous.

Transcript: Mr. Diamond, I suppose you've been dealing with bank regulators for most of your adult life. Do you believe that the US banking regulators have the statutory authority to determine how quickly America transitions to a low-carbon economy? I do not. I don't either. That's your authority, yes. That's the way I see it, but here's one of my concerns and I'm concerned about enormous power that some of the regulators have, especially the Fed, and power that is exercised in an opaque fashion. And so my question is, I'm not accusing anybody of the Fed of anything, but do they, as a practical matter, have the power that if they wanted to, they could effectively pressure financial institutions into directing capital where they want it. Yes, so speaking for myself, they are my judge, my jury, and my hangman. They pretty much can do what they want unless constrained by you. So yeah, if they wanted to come with ways to do some of those things, they can easily do that. Yeah. So one of the concerns that I have is the interest that some have to use the financial regulators, especially in the climate space. In Europe, of course, the ECB has broader authority than our Fed has, and they are pursuing this very aggressively. I worry that the Fed's decision to join the network of central banks and supervisors for greening the financial system and the ongoing development of these climate risk scenario analysis are a precursor to regulatory edicts or at least pressure to debank energy companies. And that would be exercising a power that they don't legally have. Let me move on to the issue of some of America's largest money managers. We know that these managers routinely vote the shares that they hold, including the shares they hold on behalf of their customers. And they do that including for those shares invested in passive index funds with $22 trillion in assets and an average of 25% of the votes at S&P 500 company shareholder meetings. A handful of asset managers can have, it seems to me, a huge impact on companies decisions. Mr. Rogers, let me ask you. Do you agree that the largest asset managers are capable of exercising significant influence over public companies? I'll rank a member. Thank you for that question. And we want to engage with all of our shareholders. I can engage with them individually, the largest and the smallest shareholder debate today. And certainly those who own more shares have more influence. Well, so one of my concerns is that the largest asset managers in the country have joined the net zero asset managers initiative. That explicitly states as its goal a stewardship and engagement strategy with a clear escalation and voting policy. That is consistent with our ambition for all assets under management to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. Here's the problem. These large asset managers have enormous sway by virtue of the volume of votes they can cast, even though they don't even really own many of those shares. And of course, control, if that sway goes to the level of control, then there are significant ramifications. Legal and regulatory, especially if that control is exercised over financial institutions. So I have my staff looking into this issue with the intent of producing a report on this later. Mr. Demchek, there are folks, including prominent regulators who seem to believe that large regional banks, although not as big as G-Sibs, are already too big to be resolved in the event of a crisis. And therefore, they just have to be sold to one of the other banks representing at this table. But correct me if I'm wrong. Is it true that your bank is required to submit a resolution plan to the Fed and the FDIC every three years? Yes, we've done so for 10 years. Okay. Did any of those plans that you submitted contemplate as the sole resolution a government bailout or the wholesale sale to one of these other banks? No, it's pretty easy to draw circles around our regions and sell them. Now, the regulators are fully authorized to reject a submitted plan if they thought it was not credible or otherwise sufficient. Have the regulators ever rejected your plan? No. So, it seems to me that the approval of your plan is at least a tacit admission that there is a credible resolution plan that has been articulated. And so, let me make a final point here. Some seem to think that additional regulation and added capital requirements, there's no cost. So, why not? It seems to me that there is a cost of adding unnecessary capital requirements on already well capitalized institutions. Could you share with us your perspective on what's the downside of having unnecessarily high capital requirements? Well, in this instance, it would crowd out other financings that are needed in the market. It's also making it more expensive and difficult for us to lend at a time when our country needs it. Cost capital went up. Funds are being used for something other than supporting our economy. It doesn't make sense to me. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Thanks. Mr. Timmy, Senator Reed from Rhode Island is recognized. Thank you very much. I want to thank the panel for your excellent testimony. Yesterday, I thought it was there of an ounce that another 3 and a quarter percent increase in the interest rate to 3.25 percent. Let's begin again. Thank you for being here. Interest rates are going up. I'll cut to the chase. Interest rates are going up. But the positive rates, what you pay for your deposits are rarely stagnant. Very, very low. And a reason the question is making a substantial amount of money on these increased interest rates. Why are you not beginning to raise interest rates on deposits? And I'll start with Mr. Scharke. We'll go down. Senator, thank you for the question. We are beginning to raise rates. We have products that have a range of alternatives. I think up to a peak of 1.5 percent as of the other day. And as rates continue to rise, we would expect to continue to increase the rates that we pay our customers. Mr. Morniel. The rates are already increasing on deposit accounts. And that will take place as the rate structure settles in. You can look back in history and see it. And on top of that, remember that for corporates and affluent clients, they'll go and buy treasuries and other things to direct their money's moving outside the system. And so I think we spot judge it now. You'll see a low rate structure. It'll increase over time. And then people forget zero interest checking accounts or zero interest in any rate environment. That is what changes the rate calculation of many people's site. Mr. Dynan. Exactly the same as my two colleagues here. Thank you. Mr. Rosen. Yes, we have a broad range of different deposit products. Transcript: Have you ever felt stiff during those load screens matchmaking cues or game interventions? Transform these idle moments into opportunities for a quick recharge? Dynamic stretching is an active movement where your muscles and joints stretch in motion. It preps your body getting it ready to move, unlike static stretches, where you just hold a position. Why gamers should care? Improved blood circulation, sitting for extended periods can hamper blood circulation, especially in the lower extremities. By standing and moving, you facilitate better blood flow, which can help in delivering oxygen and nutrients to various body parts, including the brain. Reduce muscle stiffness, continuous gaming, can lead to muscle tightness, particularly in the neck, shoulders, back, and legs. Dynamic stretching can counteract this by promoting muscle flexibility. Boosted energy and alertness, physical movement can be invigorating. A quick stretch might provide a refreshed feeling, possibly leading to better game performance. Injury mitigation, regular movement breaks can reduce the risk of overuse injuries commonly seen in gamers, like carpal tunnel syndrome or tendonitis. Some quick dynamic stretches for load screens, arm circles, extend your arms to the side, and make small to large circular motions with both arms. Neck tilts, gently tilt your head from side to side, then move it in a nodding motion. Leg swings, hold onto a chair for balance, and swing one leg forward and backward, then side to side. Repeat with the other leg, torso twists, with feet shoulder width apart, twist your upper body to the left, and then to the right, keeping your hips stable. Shoulder shrugs, simply raise your shoulders towards your ears, then lower them down. Turn every load screen into a chance to stretch, revitalize, and level up your game and well-being. Start small by picking one or two stretches to do during each load screen. As you get accustomed to this habit, you can gradually introduce more stretches. Over time, you'll find that not only does your body feel better, but these mini-breaks can also enhance your gaming experience by providing regular mental refreshers. Start leveling up today by checking out our website, at VitalityForGamers.com or vforg.com, and join us for the greater good.

Transcript: Who changed the Sabbath? My life is spent in one long effort to escape from the common places of existence. It's a capital mistake to theorize before one has data. Incensibly, one begins to twist facts to suit theories instead of theories to suit facts. So we're going to look at the data, analyze the facts, and come to a logical conclusion at the end. After we eliminate all the other factors, the one which remains must be the truth. The game is a foot, so let's begin. But where do we begin? Isn't it obvious? We begin at the beginning. As we open the Bible, we find that the Sabbath is woven into creation, thus the heavens and the earth, and all the hosts of them were finished. And on the seventh day, God ended his work which he had done, and he rested on the seventh day, from all his work which he had done. Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it. Because in it, he rested from all his work which God had created and made. God sanctified the Sabbath as a foundational act in creation. So I did an exhaustive study of the Bible. I was looking for anything that might explain the change in the Sabbath from the seventh day to the first day of the week. I found lots of data. There are over 100 verses in the Bible to speak about the Sabbath. And I examined every single one of them. See, for the Lord has given you the Sabbath. The Sabbath was made for man and not man for the Sabbath. Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. Six days you shall labor and do all your work. But the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord your God. And they rested on the Sabbath according to the commandments. It is a sign to me and the children of Israel forever. So what not this woman? Being a daughter of Abraham, be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath. Therefore, the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations as a perpetual covenant. The Gentiles begged that these words might be preached to them the next Sabbath. And from one Sabbath to another, all flesh shall come to worship before me, says the Lord. And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuaded both Jews and Greeks. It is the Sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings. But the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath. There's nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact. And the obvious fact is, there is no record of the Sabbath ever being changed in the Bible. Yeshua kept the Sabbath. His disciples kept the Sabbath. Even Gentile converts kept the Sabbath. Yeshua even calls himself the Lord of the Sabbath, indicating that He owns it. While it's true that the early church met at home's daily, that doesn't negate the fact that they continued to keep the Sabbath. There's also even a mention of Paul preaching on the first day of the week. But the text explains it's because he has to leave on a trip the next day, indicating that it was for a special circumstance. Also, this event seems to be taking place on Saturday night, leading up to midnight, not Sunday morning. Now on the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul, ready to depart the next day, spoke to them and continued his message until midnight. We also have a record of Paul teaching Gentiles and Corinth for a year and a half. There are 52 Sabbaths in a year, plus half a year which is 26 more Sabbaths, which equals 78 Sabbaths, just in Corinth alone. The world is full of obvious things which nobody by any chance ever observes. And the second fact I learned is that the Sabbath is always on the seventh day of the week. This may seem obvious, but there are people who seem to think that Sabbath can be any day they choose. This is a terrible mistake on their part, because they're making exceptions. Never make exceptions, and exception disproves the rule. And the rule is, the Sabbath is always and only on the seventh day of the week. The third fact I ascertained in my study is that the Sabbath is an everlasting sign between God and His people. Never trust to general impressions, my boy, but concentrate yourself upon the details. What is out of the common is usually a guide rather than a hindrance. Another fact I discovered is that the Bible spoke about apostasy that would come in the church. The Spirit clearly says that in latter times some will abandon the faith and follow deceiving spirits and things taught by demons. And they will turn their ears away from the truth and be turned aside to fables. But there were also false prophets among the people, even as there will be false teachers among you who will secretly bring in destructive heresy. You therefore beloved, since you know this beforehand, beware, lest you also fall from your own steadfastness. But we just may have taken a little derailment, a little beating, that put a smack down on our emotions. But that's just it. You won't stay in this forever friend, and when this part of your journey and season is over, never forget what it felt like. It can be used and redistributed for drive, to show love to others, and for fuel for your newfound mission. You will get past this, and on your way to and through your new journey. So when you're filled, don't forget to recognize another who may be in a similar path you were once in. So I'm leaving you with this, a big hug, some love words, and with some love through time given to articulate this message for you. Transcript: Protect yourself from daily toxins, environmental hazards and even radiation exposure, with this antioxidant-based health regime. There's no question potassium iodide is indicated if someone is exposed to significant amounts of nuclear radiation. However, potassium iodide prevents the radioactive iodine from accumulating in the thyroid gland, but it won't protect against the damaging effects of other radioactive particles. More common is the daily exposure to various forms of low-level radiation. From microwave ovens to airport security scanners, those radiation sources all around us. That's why it makes sense to take a proactive, whole-body approach to protect against the cumulative effects of low-to-moderate radiation exposure. In addition to the basic health regime that most people should follow, a high potency multivitamin, multimineral, a high-quality green drink and a pharmaceutical-grade fish oil would be recommended. Some useful foods would be a good source of water-soluble fiber, such as pears, oat bran, apples and legumes. Sulphur rich foods like garlic, onions, eggs and wayprotein. Flavanoid peck fruits like blueberries, blackberries, cherries and raspberries. Fermented soy and sea vegetables. Red vegetables like carrots, sweet potatoes and yams that are full of beta-carotene. Cruciferous vegetables like broccoli, brussel sprouts and cabbage for their sulphurifane. Artechokes, beetroot, spinach, dandelion greens and herbs like turmeric, cinnamon and mustard. A flavonoid rich extract, such as green tea, grape seed, picojanoel and ginkgobaloba. Add a dose of 100 mg per day, but ideally up to 300 mg per day. The flavonoids appear to reduce the formation of clastogenic factors, and these appear in the blood of people who are exposed to radiation, and they can persist for over 30 years. These factors are associated with an increased risk of radiation in juice cancer. Noble workers, given ginkgo extract for two months, had clastogenic factors disappear from their blood. Transcript: Half of the world is vitamin D deficient, but if you're taking vitamin D, these other two very crucial vitamins and minerals have to be used in conjunction with it, or you could be harming yourself. You are not what you eat, you are what you absorb, which means you can take in a lot of vitamin D3, but your body needs to properly put it to work. The first thing that happens is the body must convert the vitamin D to a usable active form. It needs magnesium to do this. If you don't have enough magnesium, you don't convert. If you're low on magnesium and you take a lot of vitamin D3, it's only going to take you lower, which could create a bunch of other health problems like fatigue, cramping, or low energy. Once vitamin D is active in the body, one of the main things that it does is it drives calcium to the proper places, like our bones. That's why it's good for bone health. Vitamin D moves calcium into our arteries, but it requires a second helper. Vitamin K2 is responsible for picking up the delivery of calcium and delivering it to the door step of your bones. Without vitamin K2, vitamin D3 and high doses will drive calcium into the arteries and leave it there. If you don't have K2 with it, you risk the chance of hardening your arteries over time or calcifying them. So the two of those are absolutely critical to be taken together. In my opinion, the entire family of four ADE and K, the four fat soluble vitamins need to be taken together along with magnesium to get the most out of the power of all those nutrients.

All you had to do is keep your mouth shut. There is no level there that's a safe level of contamination. Fred Stone's dairy farm is contaminated with PFAS, chemicals that have been linked to serious health problems. As the cows ingest the feed and they drink the water, it gets into the cows themselves and it translates into the milk. The presence of these chemicals in the milk caused Stone to lose his dairy license, leaving his third generation family business in ruins. We don't cry of the still milk anymore. I really don't know how we're going to proceed out of this disaster. We should be thinking about how we're going to retire and how we're going to move on. Now we're trying to figure out how to help we're going to stay alive. PFAS aren't federally regulated and they're virtually everywhere used for their non-stick water-resistant qualities in waterproof clothing, stainless-istant carpet, food wrappings, cookware, and even makeup. More than 98% of Americans have some amount of PFAS in their blood or tissue. PFAS stands for her and polyplural apple substances, so they're band-made and they originated in around the 1930s. Studies have shown they are very acutely toxic. PFAS are a problem and they're a problem because they're useful chemicals so that they do something that we like, that the more we study them, the more we see adverse health impacts. Two of the most widely studied PFAS chemicals, PFOA and PFOS, have been linked to a slew of health problems, like kidney and testicular cancers. And there's evidence that suggests PFAS can have an effect on the immune system. PFAS compounds can interfere with the immune system and essentially prevent the production of antibodies in sufficient concentrations so that we can respond to infectious disease. PFAS can remain in the body for many years and scientists don't fully understand why that is, but we note that they bind to certain proteins in our bodies, which means that they can move around, they can go from organ to organ, they can hang out in our blood, they can go to other tissues, we think that's why they stick around in our bodies. There also are some hypotheses that suggest that when PFAS get to the kidney to be excreted, the kidney doesn't get rid of them, it just transports them back into our body. The reason PFAS don't easily degrade in our bodies or in the environment has to do with their chemistry. So the carbon-foring bond is one of the strongest bonds known in chemistry. And when we make these artificially and we release them to the environment, we have to expect that those bonds are not going to degrade relatively easily at all. When PFAS contaminate the natural resources that communities depend on, the result can be disastrous. That's what happened in New York, in New York, where runoff from a nearby military base containing PFAS from firefighting foam made its way into Washington Lake, contaminating the drinking water of about 30,000 people. One of our greatest assets in the city of Newburg has been contaminated, undue to any fault of our own, it makes me angry, it makes me sad, it makes me emotional because it's not fair. After the contamination came to light in 2016, the city changed its drinking water source and has been trying to remediate Washington Lake. It was 18,000 pounds vessel of the carbon, so it's granular activated carbon, 40,000 pounds per vessel. Activated carbon treatment is a method of filtering PFAS out of water. The chemicals stick to the porous carbon as the water passes through. But removing the PFAS from the drinking water still leaves the chemicals intact. So when you filter PFAS out of water, you're just taking it from here and putting it here where it's either going to be incinerated or a landfill or filtered out and put somewhere else. So that's the problem with PFAS. They just get moved around, they don't get eliminated, at least with the technologies that we have right now. Unless we do something to intervene, they'll be present for decades, if not hundreds, or thousands of years to come. My wife and I actually met showing cows together. Transcript: Brothers and sisters, let us bow our heads in prayer, Father God. We come before you today with open hearts and minds. We invite your Holy Spirit to fill this place. Guide my words, Lord. Let them be your words, spoken through me. Open our hearts to receive your message. In Jesus' name we pray, amen. We turn your Bibles to the Book of Revelation, chapter 21. This chapter is one of the most profound and awe-inspiring passages in the entire Bible. It speaks of a future that is beyond our wildest dreams, a future that God has prepared for those who love it. Today, we're going to delve into the glorious vision of a new heaven and a new earth. Imagine a world where the beauty of a sunrise over majestic mountains is just a glimpse of the splendor that awaits us. A world where the sky is always bright, and the clouds are always filled with light. This ain't just some far off fairy tale, y'all. This is a promise, a divine assurance that transcends time and space. It's a reality that is more real than the ground we stand on. It's a future that God himself has promised to bring to pass. This is the very word of God, a promise he made to each and every one of us. When we hold the Bible close to our hearts, we are holding on to the promises of God. When we raise our hands in worship, we are reaching out to the one who holds our future in his hands. In Revelation John the disciple whom Jesus loved, was given a glimpse of this glorious future. Imagine being on the island of Patmos exiled and alone and then being given a vision so magnificent that it changes the course of history. John saw what many of us can only dream of. He saw a new heaven and a new earth where sin and sorrow were no more. Picture a world where the landscapes are lush and green, where rivers flow peacefully, and where the environment is serene and untouched by the pain and suffering of this world. This vision wasn't just for John, it's for all of us who believe in his name. It's a vision that unites us, a vision that brings people from all walks of life together in prayer and worship. It's a vision that gives us hope and a future. It's a beacon of hope, a light at the end of the tunnel. Just as a lighthouse guides ships safely to shore, this vision guides us through the darkest times in our lives. It reminds us that no matter how dark the night, the light of God's promise will always shine through. It's a place where children can play freely, where the elderly can walk hand in hand without fear. A place where love and joy are the order of the day, and where every tear is wiped away. This is the new heaven and new earth that God has promised us. As we look up at the starry night sky, let us remember that the same God who created the stars has also prepared a place for us, a place where we will dwell with Him forever. In perfect peace and harmony, this is our hope, this is our future, this is the promise of a new heaven and a new earth. John describes a magnificent city descending from heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. This vision, as described in the book of Revelation, is one of the most awe-inspiring and hopeful images in the entire Bible. Imagine a city so pure, so holy, that it is likened to a bride on her wedding day, radiant and full of promise. This my friends is the holy city, the new Jerusalem, our eternal dwelling place. It is a place where we will find everlasting peace and joy, a sanctuary where sorrow and pain are no more. The new Jerusalem is not just a city, it is a symbol of God's ultimate promise to us, a promise of eternal life and unending happiness. Can you imagine a city so dazzling, so breathtakingly beautiful, that it could only have been created by the hand of God Himself? This is a place where the beauty is beyond our wildest dreams, a testament to God's infinite creativity and love. This city ain't like any city we know here on earth. Our earthly cities with all their marvels and advancements, pale in comparison to the new Jerusalem. Here there are no skyscrapers casting shadows, no pollution clouding the skies, no noise disrupting the tranquility. It is a city of perfect harmony and divine order. It's a place of unimaginable splendor, where the streets are paved with gold. These golden streets are not just a symbol of wealth but of purity and holiness. They reflect the light of God's glory, guiding us in our eternal journey. And the gates are made of pearl. Each gate, a single pearl, stands as a testament to the beauty and perfection of God's creation. These gates are always open, welcoming all who are worthy to enter and partake in the eternal blessings of this divine city. It's a city where there's no need for the sun or the moon because the glory of God illuminates it completely. Imagine a place where the light never fades, where the warmth of God's presence is felt at all times. This divine illumination is a constant reminder of God's love and grace, a light that guides us and keeps us safe for all eternity. Imagine brothers and sisters walking down streets paved with pure gold. Imagine gazing upon walls made of jasper and sapphire, gates of pearl, and foundations adorned with every precious stone imaginable. The beauty of this city is beyond our wildest dreams, but this city ain't just about physical beauty, y'all. It's about the presence of God. The Bible tells us that the throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it. We will finally be in the presence of our Creator face to face for all eternity. Section 5, a prayer for renewal, embracing God's promises. Let us pray, Father. We thank You for the hope that we have in Your promises. Help us to truly grasp the magnitude of Your love and the glory that awaits us. Renew our spirits, Lord, and fill us with Your peace. In Jesus' name, amen. Sometimes life can get us down. We might feel lost, alone or afraid. But we must always remember that this world is not our home. We're just passing through on our way to that glorious city that heavenly home prepared for us. Section 6, God's dwelling place, our intimate relationship with the divine. In this new heaven and new earth, God Himself will dwell among His people. Can you imagine that, y'all? The God of all creation, living among us, walking with us, talking with us, just like He did with Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden. That's ain't just about proximity. It's about intimacy. We will finally have the close personal relationship with God that we were always meant to have. No more separation, no more barriers, just pure, unadulterated fellowship with our creator. Section 7, no more tears, no more pain, the ultimate healing. In a world filled with so much suffering and heartache, the promise of ultimate healing is a beacon of hope. There's a promise that transcends time and space, offering solace to those who are weary and burdened. One of the most beautiful promises in Revelation 21 is that God will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Imagine the comfort in knowing that every sorrow, every heartache, every moment of despair will be tenderly addressed by a loving creator. This is not just a fleeting comfort, but an eternal assurance. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain. For the old order of things has passed away. Picture a world where the cycle of life and death is no longer a source of fear or sadness, a world where the beauty of creation is fully restored, unmarred by the shadows of suffering. Can you imagine a life without tears, without pain, without the sting of death? It is a vision so profound that it almost seems beyond our grasp, yet it is a promise given to us, a glimpse into a future where all things are made new, a future where peace and joy are the norm, not the exception. This is the promise we cling to, especially when we're hurting, when we're grieving, when we feel like our hearts can't possibly bear another ounce of pain. In those moments of deep sorrow, this promise becomes our anchor, our source of strength. It reminds us that our suffering is not in vain, that there is a greater purpose and a greater hope. God sees our suffering and He promises to make all things new. He is not distant or indifferent to our pain. He is intimately aware of every tear, every cry, every moment of anguish, and He promises that one day all of this will be transformed. The ultimate healing is not just a future event, but a present reality that we can hold on to, a promise that gives us the courage to face each day with hope and faith. Section 8 The Book of Life and Invitational to Eternal Belonging Now, some folks might be wondering, how do I know if I'll be a part of this new heaven and new earth? Well, the Bible tells us that those whose names are written in the Lamb's Book of Life will enter the city. The Lamb, of course, is Jesus Christ, who sacrificed Himself for our sins. Accepting Him as our Lord and Savior is the key to having our names written in that book. It's an invitation to eternal belonging, a guarantee that we will spend eternity in the presence of our Savior. Section 9 Closing prayer, gratitude and hope for the future. Let us close with a prayer of gratitude. Father, we thank you for the hope we have in your promises. Thank you for the vision of a new heaven and a new earth where your glory shines brightly and your presence brings us comfort and peace. Help us to live each day with that hope in our hearts, knowing that you are preparing a place for us. In Jesus' name, we pray, amen. Remember brothers and sisters this life is fleeting but the promises of God are eternal. Section 10 Call to action, spreading the good news. If this message has touched your heart today, I encourage you to share it with others. Like this video, subscribe to our channel, and click that notification bell so you never miss a message of hope and encouragement. Your assignment for this week is to tell someone about Jesus and donate to your local food pantry. Together, we can all help feed the world one mouth at a time. The same as Jesus who fed 5,000 with two fish and five loaves of bread. If we all give a little, it will be a great amount. Consider joining us in person for church on Sundays at 9.45am at 539 Montana Road, Phillips Berk, New Jersey, 08865.

Firstly, many men find it challenging to transition from a structured working life to the freedom of retirement. Another key issue is financial instability. Many men find themselves in a precarious position due to inadequate savings and poor retirement planning. A significant part of their income goes into supporting their families, often neglecting their own future needs. So how can these challenges be addressed? If possible, avoid getting second wife or another young family just because you got a boom of retirement benefits at your 60 years of age. Also make sure you have your own retirement home besides that have a medical plan or a health insurance that can sustain you in old age. Make sure you have a healthy relationship with your immediate family. The other tip is about investment which is a crucial step. Starting from the first day of work, men should consider savings and investment plans. It's not just about securing financial stability but also creating a safety net for old age. Education is another essential aspect. Equip your children with quality education so they can stand on their own feet reducing your financial burden in the long run. Retirement planning is a journey of self-discovery. Understand your relationship with money, your tolerance for risk and your discipline in the face of uncertainty. The earlier you start this journey, the smoother your transition to retirement will be. Another solution is to discuss retirement. Talk about it, plan for it, envision it. Create a vision board that reminds you of your retirement goals. In conclusion, the struggle that men face in retirement can be attributed to a lack of preparation, both financially and psychologically. By investing early, planning for retirement and shifting their identity away from their work roles, men can enjoy a more fulfilling and less stressful retirement. Remember, it's not just about surviving in retirement, it's about thriving, exploring new passions and enjoying the fruits of your lifelong labour. Start planning today for a better tomorrow. Comment and subscribe to make this channel grow and get more insights in future.

You know if you're sitting in a chair watching this video right now, you're burning roughly about one calorie per minute. But when we strength train, we can increase this to about 20 or even 30 calories per minute. You see muscle is the major site where we burn carbs and fats. So when we eat a meal, about 80% of the food that is ingested is distributed to the muscle. When muscle begins to fail or when we develop problems with our muscles, it is not surprising that we develop a range of diseases associated with that. Have you heard of sarcopenia? It means poverty of strength or loss of muscle mass. And we don't just wake up one day and we're in this situation. It does progress over time. And after our age 30, we lose 3 to 8% of our muscle mass every decade. There was a study done where they compared under a microscope across section of a 40-year old thigh to a 75-year-old athlete's thigh muscle. And they looked almost identical. Amazing. You see muscle knows no age, so we can't use that excuse. The old saying is still true if you don't use it, you lose it. But the good news is, muscle wasting can be reversed through strength training. There was another study done on an 85-year-old person who focused just on strengthening their legs for 12 weeks and they noticed a 40% increase in the thigh muscle. According to the research, lifting weights and increasing muscle mass can reduce risk factors for some of the most common diseases and leading causes of death and keep you functioning well into your latter years by improving your bone health and preventing debilitating breaks, improving your sense of balance, keeping you from falling and improving your flexibility so you don't have to ask your family members to do the unthinkable. While sarcopenia and muscle loss as you age is a real problem, it is still totally possible to build muscle as you get older, as long as you lift weights a few times per week. And you know friends, you can be your own gym. My advice would be to master your body weight first and then grab the weights. Invest in a personal trainer to get you started and give you a solid foundation. Again, we need to think about muscle as medicine. Muscle is so much more than looking nice and trim, although that's an added benefit. It's more than athletic performance. Muscle is our body armor. Muscle is our site for energy metabolism and muscle will augment a robust immune system. It has been said, the more healthy muscle mass you have, the greater your survivability against nearly every disease. You know friends, we are living in a very unique time in history. Jesus says in Matthew 11, 28-30, come onto me, all of you who are weary and heavy laden and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you and learn of me. For I am gentle and lowly in heart and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is easy and my burden is light. Transcript: The Lives of the Saints by Father Alben Butler August 13th St. Cassian, martyr. He was a Christian schoolmaster and taught children to read and write, at Emola, a city 27 miles from Ravenna in Italy, a violent persecution being raised against the church, probably that of Diceus or Valerian, or according to some that of Julian. He was taken up and interrogated by the governor of the province. As he constantly refused to sacrifice to the gods, the barbarous judge, having informed himself of what profession he was, commanded that his own scholars should stab him to death with their iron writing pencils, called styles. For at that time, it was the custom for scholars to write upon wax laid on a board of box and wood, in which they formed the letters with an iron style or pencil, sharp at one end, but blunt and smooth at the other, to erase what was to be a face or corrected. They also often wrote on box and wood itself, as St. Ambrose mentions, the smaller the instruments were, and the weaker the executioners, the more lingering and cruel was this martyr's death. He was exposed naked in the midst of 200 boys, among whom some, through their tablets, pencils, and pen knives at his face and head, and often broke them upon his body. Bars cut his flesh or stabbed him with their pen knives, and others pierced him with their pencils, sometimes only tearing the skin and flesh and sometimes raking in his very bowels. Some made it their barbarous sport to cut part of their writing task in his tender skin. Thus covered with his own blood and wounded in every part of his body, he cheerfully bade his little executioners not to be afraid, and to strike him with greater force. Not meaning to encourage them in their sin, but to express the ardent desire he had to die for Christ. He was interred by the Christians at Imola, where afterward his relics were honored with a rich mausoleum. Prudentius tells us that in his journey to Rome, he visited this holy martyr's tomb, and prostrate before it implored the divine mercy for the pardon of his sins with many tears. He mentions a moving picture of this saint's martyrdom hanging over the altar, representing his cruel death in the manner he has recorded it in verse. He exhorts all others with him to commend their petitions to this holy martyr's patronage, who fails not to hear pious supplications.

He automatically assumed that I meant that it meant a 15 degree per hour rotation of the globe. It absolutely was not earth rotation. We sent it to him. He chose not to use it and he chose to portray us as if we had detected rotation of the Earth. He betrayed my partner, Geron. By basically taking an out of sequence part of it, putting it at the end of a film and it was just completely out of sequence misrepresented. But what he made it look like was that they had just measured curvature and Geron's going, oh, interesting. Absolutely deceitful, despicable behavior, Daniel. What we did is in Colorado, we went to a place called Pike's Peak. Pike's Peak is 14,125 feet in elevation. We got that measure, meant, okay. And then what we did is we went to do east down to the plains of Colorado and about a 10,000 foot elevation drop. And we did another measurement. Transcript: Hello everyone. Today we are going to talk about one of the most common questions in the world of health. How does our body get energy? We all know that we need energy to keep moving, to think, to breathe and to do all our daily activities. But where does that energy come from? We start. Let's get to the point. The two main sources of energy are sugars and fats. Sugar is our simple carbohydrates found in many foods such as fruits, vegetables, bread, pasta, sweets and soft drinks. Fats, on the other hand, are a denser source of energy found in foods such as oil, butter, nuts and meat. After we consume food, our bodies break down carbohydrates and fats into smaller molecules and use them for energy. Carbohydrates are converted into glucose, which is a quick source of energy for our body. Fats, on the other hand, are converted into fatty acids and glycerol, which provide a longer lasting source of energy. So, which of these two energy sources is the more recommended? Well, the answer depends on the activity we are doing. If we are doing a short, intense activity, such as lifting weights or running at high speed, then carbohydrates are the preferred energy source. Carbohydrates provide a quick source of energy that our body can use immediately. On the other hand, if we are doing a more moderate, long-lasting activity, such as yoga or walking, then fats are the preferred energy source. Fats provide a longer lasting source of energy that our body can use for longer periods of time. But remember, not all carbohydrates and fats are the same. It is important to choose healthy sources of energy, such as fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, healthy fats such as olive oil and avocado, and complex carbohydrates. Such as those found in whole grains. In addition, we cannot forget the importance of water in obtaining energy. Our bodies need water to transport nutrients and oxygen to our cells and to eliminate waste. And that's all for today. I hope you enjoyed this video. If you liked it, don't forget to like it and share it with your friends. And if you have any questions or comments, leave them in the comments section below, see you in the next video. I'll leave you a link to the best sources of nutrition. Thank you for watching.
