Transcript: Hi, and welcome to CGS Tech. A reliable shelter is an essential human requirement. It provides its comfort, security, and protection. Earthquakes, natural disasters, and wars can leave many people displaced, while an economic downturn and unforesee circumstances like a pandemic can create a homelessness crisis. Responding to a disaster or a crisis requires fast, easy, and cost-effective solutions. In this video, we'll take a look at some innovative shelter solutions that can provide relief to those in need. Alaskan-based Inter Shelter offers a quick and cost-effective shelter solution for a multitude of situations like emergency relief, home-less housing, camping, getaway, or military post. Their shelter's feature at dome-shaped design consisting of hard-sighted composite panels. Inter shelter dome is a frameless structure, with the strength of a standard building, but the mobility of a tent. One dome can be assembled by two people in less than four hours, with nothing more than a screwdriver, wrench, and a step ladder. Inter shelter's 50-year lifespan and ability to withstand 40 feet of snow in 160-mile-an-hour winds make it well-suited for difficult climates. Domes can be equipped with every component needed for a comfortable stay, including a kitchen, shower, loft, and off-grid systems. They are available in two sizes, 14 feet in diameter with 154 square foot floor space, and 20 feet in diameter with 314 square foot floor space. Amplighting from the windows and glass doors keeps the interior bright. The cost of the larger version is about $12,000 for the shell, plus add-on costs for the flooring system, insulation, and so on. When assembled in a group, the Inter shelter creates a tight-knit community of domed homes that can be connected to make larger layouts. The company was established in 1992 with the desire to get homeless veterans off the streets, and her sheltered domes have come a long way since then, and are now being used extensively in the hospitality sector. Better Shelter is a collaborative effort between the Ikea Foundation and the United Nations Refugee Agency, intending to create durable, low-cost, and rapidly deployable shelters for people displaced by conflicts and natural disasters around the world. It offers a dignified and weatherproof home for displaced people and a cost-effective solution for humanitarian organizations. Since 2015, over 65,000 of them have been provided to refugee camps, transit sites, and emergencies in over 70 countries across the world. Better Shelter is designed to be shipped flat-packed in two cardboard boxes, and then assembled on-site. All the necessary tools and instructions come included. It can be installed in 5-6 hours by a team of 4 people with minimum site preparation and no electricity required. The unit measures 17.5 square meters or 188 square feet in size. The structures steal frame as securely anchored to the ground and clad with tough yet lightweight roof and wall panels made of polyolifant foam treated with UV protection. The unit includes four windows, four ventilation openings, and a lockable door. A solar panel on the roof generates power to illuminate a built-in lamp, as well as power for the charging of electronic devices. The modular design of the better shelter also enables alterations in size and layout. Sections can be added and removed to create different size facilities. The shelter can be disassembled, moved, and reassembled. The shelter's expected lifespan is three years with basic maintenance. The current cost of a unit is 1,150 euros, or about 1,360 US dollars. The shelter can also come in a frame-only version, simply called Structure. The metal framework can be covered with a tarp and serve as an emergency shelter in the immediate aftermath of a disaster or a conflict. Over time, as communities recover, structure can be upgraded with local materials by residents themselves, enabling incremental upgrading adaptable to different climates, building traditions, and norms. Shift pods are heavy-duty pop-up shelters great for festivals, camping, guest rooms, emergency relief, and refugee camps. They utilize latest space-age composite fabrics and a special seam ceiling technology to make them element-resistant and to provide a comfortable stay even in harsh conditions. Designed for the heat of the desert, the shift pod works equally well in the snow. Reflective fabrics keep the heat out and the warmth of your body in, while it is still cold out. These four season shelters are built to last and provide years of comfort while having tent-like mobility and ease of use. The latest iteration, shift pod 3, is built on an integrated carbon fiber frame and hub system, allowing for a quick setup and making it robust. The special all-season multi-layered fabric system, is heat reflective and insulated with mildew protection and hydrophobic coatings to protect against the elements. Standard shift pod 3 stands at 6 feet 8 inches tall in the center and with 107 square foot floor space. Shift pods come in XL and mini versions as well. At about 50 pounds overall for the standard version, shift pod is lightweight and comes self-contained with integrated poles. It can be set up and taken down by just one person in mere minutes. Other features include convection vents, fine mesh bug screens on six windows and two doors, storage pockets, ports for power cords, and more. Shift pods XL can be connected together with a tunnel system. At the time of making this video, standard shift pod 3 goes for about $1,500. For every 20 units sold, the company contributes one unit to a charity cause. The Humana Hut Shelter System is a rapidly deployable accommodation solution that provides shelter, safety, and comfort to emergency service workers like firefighters, to refugees and those affected by natural disasters, or housing to remote working environments. The Humana Hut was initially conceived in 2013 as a solution to the growing humanitarian crisis created by the Syrian Civil War. Since then, the Humana Hut system has developed into a complete field infrastructure system, not just for humanitarian purposes, but for any kind of field accommodation needs. The base unit, Humana Hut is a foldable box that can be packed in numbers into a shipping container, and then deployed on site. Shipping containers are repurposed as a bathroom unit, utility room, community space, and storage facility. Each Humana Hut can sleep up to eight people, and has power and water hookups, a table, benches, sink, and heating. It is insulated and can withstand harsh weather conditions. A unit can be erected in five minutes by a small team and a forklift. These pop-up foldable containers are quick and easy to set up or pack up, while sleeping a minimal environmental footprint. Structures are strong, rigid, and climate controlled, and having a 20-year lifespan, a Humana Hut system proves to be more cost-effective in the long run compared to alternatives such as prefabricated buildings and tents. Because the utilities are all above ground, ground preparation is usually not necessary. The Humana Hut field infrastructure system can be installed on soft or hard ground, and can utilize power from any source. Power can be grid-connected or off-grid with a generator, and there are renewable options available. Palette is a social purpose enterprise with a mission to provide access to housing and employment for those experiencing homelessness, with its low cost and effective shelter solutions. For more than half a million people facing homelessness across the United States, the Palette shelters can provide a stepping stone into a life of stability. Palette shelter is a personal, safe, and dignified basic accommodation space that can be put up in a matter of hours, made in the USA of durable aluminum frame, and composite panel materials with a 10-plus-year lifespan. Panels are mold, rot, and pest resistant, and easy to clean and repair. The units are flat-packed, so as many as 30 shelters per truck can be shipped to their assembly destination. They can be assembled with minimal tools, on-sites ranging from parking lots to grassy fields. Palette shelters feature a structural aluminum floor, which serves as a built-in foundation, eliminating the need for any foundation work. Units are secured to the ground usually by staking. Shelters can come in varying levels of insulation, and are already outfitted with pull-down beds, climate control, safety features, electricity, and more to be ready for residents to move in. A locking door provides security and peace of mind, allowing residents to lock their personal belongings, and leave their shelter to engage in their community, access jobs, and participate in other crucial activities. The units come in two sizes, a 64-square-feet two-bed unit, with a starting price of $5,500. And a 100-square-feet four-bed unit, starting at about $9,000. Palette shelters are designed without a kitchen or a bathroom, because they are intended to be used in a community setting, where these facilities exist on site. Another reason is that the plumbing is expensive to build, and maintain, and would drive up the price substantially. Although the company is currently prototyping a version with a bathroom, a larger community room, and kitchen facility as well, Palette currently does not sell any of its units to one-off customers. All employees who build palette shelters are formally homeless, addicted, or incarcerated themselves, and have found stability through meaningful employment, living wage pay, and a supportive environment. The Maggi shelter is a sturdy, highly insulated, sustainable shelter that is adaptable to all climates. It is a new type of temporary shelter that is set up like a tent, but acts like a building. This is achieved by a double-layered skin that can be filled with local materials like sand, to create an insulation layer. The Maggi shelter is designed to serve communal activities, medical facilities, schools, community centers, and temperature-controlled warehouses. In these uses, the shelter can foster education and community, and provide clean and safe spaces for medical treatment and supply storage. The shelter comes as a building kit package that can be set up by six adults in two days. All the parts can be mounted from the ground up, no cranes or heavy tools are needed. The frame is made with extruded aluminum profiles, protected against outdoor influences by tough polyester fabric sheets that serve as walls and a roof. The fabric is coated with fire retardant. Windows are made with two layers of transparent fabric, with insulating layers of bubble wrap in between. The hollow walls and roof of the Maggi are filled with local insulating materials, such as straw, sand, or even plastic waste. The Maggi shelter controls inside temperature by using mass inertia of materials like sand and light insulation boards. Sand stabilizes temperature fluctuations between day and night, and the insulation boards keep the optimal temperature inside once achieved. The Maggi can be upgraded with a fixed floor that uses the same aluminum profiles as the rest of the structure. Between the beams, the floor can also be insulated with local materials or other insulation. Heating comes in the form of a standard wood burning stove, while small windows offer some natural light and ventilation. The shelter is also modular and can be joined with other units to increase available space. Thanks for watching. Another video on Pre-Fab Shelters coming soon. Stay tuned, until next time.

Transcript: I just thought to myself, how would I want to live if I was in that situation? That's how it came out. I mean, I knew nothing about a tiny home at anything. You know, once we started putting these up, it's like everybody is starting to cry. Oh, what made you tiny houses? I don't know. I know that's how I would like to live that way if I was at. And that's why these men do so well here. For Carmen Guidi, however, building the second-wind cottages, a small collection of nine tiny houses on his property in Newfeld, just five miles outside of Ithaca, was divinely inspired after good will trips to Honduras in Haiti. The Autobody Repair Tech created the Cottage Village as a nonprofit, and private donations and volunteers helped build each $15,000 home. Unlike a shelter or group home, Guidi says the cottages meet a crucial need for the homeless. They give the men a level of dignity that they can't get anywhere else. They take ownership, which is very important, I think, to take an ownership, even though they don't own the houses. They still take an ownership. They take pride around the surroundings. Here's the thing. They want to stay in community. They want to be in community, but yes, they want to have their own time to in their own space. The cottages are like autonomous studio apartments, allowing each resident to regain a sense of normalcy with their own kitchen, their own bathroom and living space, and some even keeping pets in their home. So far, second-win only serves homeless men, although Guidi hopes to expand the project to include individual housing for women and children at a separate location. While he's not a professional social worker, Guidi has been reaching out to and building relationships with Ithaca's homeless for years. A lot of the times when people are put into the program type models, they feel like a project. They feel like a project. They don't feel like a project. Just off of Ithaca's main commercial boulevard, behind a popular multinational discount department store, is a field of overgrown underbrush and a thicket of trees. It's become an unofficial campground. Most people might not notice it at all, but to the homeless of Ithaca and the Greater Tomkins County, it's well known as the jungle. Guidi makes frequent trips to the area. They don't know. There was someone staying under that tarp. I don't know if there's anyone near now or now. He says most of the relationships he's built start with him offering food or supplies, and eventually he's able to convince some to move into the second-win cottages. That's Bill's spot down there. He says one of the most shocking things he's learned is how many homeless people simply cannot afford to live any other way. It's work. He works every day. He works every single day. The jungle may look desolate and bleak, but that's not where all of the homeless in Ithaca find themselves. Nell's bond, director of Ithaca's urban renewal agency, says the city successfully houses most of their homeless. The unsheltered population, including those who live in the jungle, are only about 15 to 20 people. I think we pretty well know most of our homeless persons by first name and understand their needs a little bit better because we have the advantage of being so small. The disadvantage is once we fill up our emergency shelter or our Magnolia house project, we don't have any more room. There's just limited capacity. As a smaller city, Ithaca has about 40 emergency shelters. A new shelter called Magnolia project for women and children and about 100 permanent supportive housing units. Bond says the city is supportive of Guidi's second-win project, but addressing the issue means more than just a roof over their heads and food on the table. Building a facility by itself probably won't solve all the needs because people come with a lot of issues that they have to work through. They work their way down to homelessness and need to work their way back out of homelessness and success. The support services is always an area where there's not enough funding to really address the need in our opinion. Everything from addiction to mental health to job training and family crisis services are all offered to people in need through state and federal agencies. And Bond says Guidi has begun to work with them to better serve the second-win residents. Carmen has taken with second-win cottages, has really taken it on himself and internalized a lot of the challenges that an organization would have. I don't think he's done it by himself. I mean, there has been support from another group working with them. And I think he's open to that and has learned that there's some good resources out there, but working through state and federal funding processes is laborious for somebody who is not interested in the paperwork side of it. Both men agree that for anyone to begin to address homelessness in a metropolis like New York City or in smaller cities upstate like Ithaca, it first has to begin with affordable housing for everyone. According to the Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance, which offers housing and support services, Governor Cuomo is currently proposing a five-year, $20 billion investment. Half will go to build 100,000 units of affordable housing across the state, and the other half will be used to build out the state supportive services and 20,000 beds to go with them. As for the second-win cottages, Guidi is already working on adding nine more with the main house that can accommodate some of the state services that are needed. So far, there is no timeline on how long each resident can stay, and the longest have been there for three years. The city of Ithaca has also helped Guidi attain rental funds for the men, but even as they expand, the second-win cottages already has a waiting list of almost 30 people. In Ithaca, I'm Jennifer Flanagan for the Innovation Trail.

Transcript: The death of critical thinking. Critical thinking does not require intelligence so much as intellectual honesty. Of course, intelligence matters, as it does with everything. But the most important factor is honesty. It's not just an honesty with others. It starts as an honesty with yourself. I think of critical thinking as a religious like adherence to facts, only to facts, and to all of the facts relevant in any situation. If you want to see what critical thinking is not, then listen to the meandering of any politicians, and most others in public life today. These people count on us not to be critical, honest thinkers. That's why most of us resent them, even though many of us don't quite know why. Critical thinking is an objective need of human functioning, and ultimately survival. When we encounter people who are disingenuous, we often sense it, and, if we're even a little bit survival oriented, we recoil against it. It's a healthy, rational reaction, although not always a well-understood one, since so many of us are not introspective and self-reflective. When you're a critical thinker, you're not subject to fake news. You won't accept anything where the facts don't add up. You'll demand proof of any claim. You won't provide claims with too easy a pass for acceptance. You'll spot the glaring evasions or the absurd hypocrisy, not because of a high IQ, although that helps, but because you're confident in your mind and possess a religious-like reverence for truth. Critical thinking is more than a skill. It's an attitude. It applies across the board. It comes up in your personal relationships, your business relationships, even in a short conversation with a stranger. You don't, and will not, pretend to accept what you know isn't true. If you're a critical thinker, people know where they stand with you. It's possible you'll be wrong, but you're honest. When you embody the phrase, say what you mean and mean what you say. You're being a critical thinker. Critical thinking is a rarity in any era. Today it's almost nonexistent. Intellectual, moral and psychological fraud is all around us, not just in the media and government, but in our personal and social relations as well. It's sad, and it's not human nature, but it has become the norm. People still think critically on the inside, but on the outside it almost seems like a desperate need to show how you're not thinking. I'm not judgmental. Is a statement of pride, as if judgment itself were a subject of shame. You might as well be saying, I'm mindless and proud of it. It's insanity for people who can and should be sane, and getting more insane every day. The best thing to do for yourself and such an environment? Refuse to be that way. Refuse 247. You will attract the right people and repel the wrong ones. If everyone is repulsive, so be it. Eventually you will always find one or two of the right ones. Maybe someday the right way of using your mind will become the norm. The beautiful thing is that you can do it all by yourself if you must, and nobody can ever take it away from you. Whether you're a religious believer or an atheist, your mind is your temple. It's your means of survival. It's your basis for self-esteem, for enjoying your emotions, for everything.

We are probably one of the last generations of homo sapiens. Within a century or two, Earth will be dominated by entities that are more different from us than we are different from the Andotals or from chimpanzees. And if too many of the machines became concentrated in two few hands, humanity split into classes, into capitalists and polytariots. Now data is replacing machinery as the most important asset. Until today, nobody had the necessary computing power and the necessary data to hack humanity. But this is now changing because of two simultaneous revolutions. In the 21st century, new technological revolutions, especially AI and machine learning, might swing the pendulum in the opposite direction. And if democracy cannot adapt to these new conditions, the newmen will come to live under the rule of digital dictatorships. Transcript: Can we engineered the weather? Cloud seating is a form of weather modification that can produce what we want more or less of, more rain or snow, or even smaller hail pellets. China is building the world's largest weather modification system to artificially enhance rain that will cover an area of over 2.1 million square miles by 2025. Today at least 52 countries across the globe are using some sort of weather modification program. While it may sound too good to be true, the technology has been around for more than 75 years. Clouds are made up of tiny water droplets. Groups of droplets form water vapor or ice crystals. By itself, this water vapor is intense enough to fall to the ground as precipitation. Instead, it rises until it becomes super cool and condenses, around tiny particles of dust in the sky called condensation nuclei. It takes billions of these condensed water droplets to form a visible cloud. In cloud seating, a seating agent is used as the condensation nuclei. Global seating agents are chemicals such as silver iodide, potassium iodide, or solid carbon dioxide. These are shot into clouds by rockets or sprayed into clouds using drones or aircraft. Unattached super cooled water vapor molecules in the clouds condense around these particles. The condensed water vapor droplets then group together, becoming larger and heavier. This process continues until the droplets are large enough to fall as rain. Recently the UAE created artificial rain using drones. These drones targeted certain clouds with electrical discharges through concentrated lasers to force water droplets to pool in the air, triggering the desired rainfall. Today the largest cloud seating system in the world is found in China. China creates 55 billion tons of artificial rain a year. Other countries are also looking to ramp up cloud seating efforts in the hope of increasing precipitation. Thailand has an ambitious aim to remove water shortages in 98% of the country's drought-affected areas by 2037. The idea behind cloud seating is to create rain in regions that are most affected by droughts, thus reducing the impact of droughts. In 2015, cloud seating increased the local rainfall in Texas by about 34%. The technology can also be used to manage hail. According to an estimate, hail storms in the U.S. cause an average of $15 billion in damage to homes, cars and crops each year. Cloud seating increases the number of ice pellets in hail producing clouds, but decreases the size of each pellet. This can reduce the damage caused by hail. Cloud seating can also clear away fog by turning it into precipitation, improving visibility around airports. But there is a catch for cloud seating to work. Specific atmospheric conditions must exist. Cloud seating can't create clouds. It can only add particles to clouds which interact with the water vapor already present in the air. So cloud seating does not always go as planned. In 2009, China performed cloud seating in an attempt to end a drought, resulting in a temperature drop and a snowstorm that closed roads around Beijing. There are also concerns about unwanted ecological changes. Rain in one area might bring drought to another, which could lead to ecological imbalances. After all, water that falls from the sky must go somewhere. If that extra precipitation falls in a place where it cannot be absorbed into the ground, then it could trigger flooding. Today water shortages and floods affect every continent. Around 1.2 billion people, or almost one fifth of the world's population, live in water scare serious. Another 500 million people face intermittent scarcity, and around 1.47 billion are directly exposed to the risk of intense flooding. While cloud seating is not a permanent solution, it may help to reduce the number of those affected.

And when I'm winning, you'll watch, I'm not greedy at all. I'm locking in my profits, I'm very systematic. Right? I'm not looking at the stocks going to go much higher. Transcript: I think the concepts, I have, I teach a lot of keystone concepts, concepts that are more universal in theory. And a professionalism is synonymous with value as a good example. The tree of life stands on each side of the river a symbol of eternal sustenance. It bears 12 kinds of fruit, yielding its fruit every month, a testament to God's provision. The leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations, bringing peace and restoration. This imagery reminds us of the Garden of Eden, a place of perfect harmony. It is a place of abundance and healing, where every need is met. As we reflect on these verses, we see God's promise of restoration, a promise that is both comforting and inspiring. He will make all things new, bringing forth a new creation. He will bring us back to a place of perfection, a place where we can dwell with Him forever. This message is a reminder that God's promises are reliable, a beacon of truth in the world of uncertainty. We can trust in His Word, knowing that it is a firm foundation for our lives. The angel also said, we hold I am coming soon, a declaration that fills us with both urgency and hope. Blessed is He who keeps the words of the prophecy in this book. It is a reminder that we must live according to God's Word, embodying its principles in our daily lives. We must be prepared for His return, living each day with a sense of readiness and expectation. This message is relevant to us today, speaking directly to our contemporary context and challenges. We are called to keep the words of the prophecy, ensuring that they guide our thoughts and actions. We are called to live in a way that honors God, reflecting His love and truth in all we do. We are called to be ready for His return, maintaining a posture of alertness and spiritual preparedness. It can remind us of his love and grace. Let us take a moment to enjoy this music. Let it be a time of reflection and worship. Feel the presence of God as you listen. Let his peace fill your heart. Let his love surround you. This is a time to connect with him. This is a time to be still and know that he is God. Thank you for being here today. Thank you for being part of this journey. May God bless you and keep you. May his face shine upon you and give you peace. Go in peace and may the love of God be with you always. Amen. My brothers, as we transition into the next year, I would just like to encourage you all to keep going forward on your path with the freedom. I don't say they aforementioned lightly because of the complex nature of what we all face as free men who embrace the Mektao philosophy. However, my brothers, it is where we are all going, both individually as well as corporately, which makes it vitally important that we not only keep going forward, but as well keep looking forward in the direction of where we are all going. My brothers, here is an analogy of what I am talking about. When I was attending CCY in New York, I would often take the No. 1 subway train to get to a certain part of the college campus. Sometimes, if the train was not crowded, I would stand by the doors to look out the door windows to see the sights as soon as the train exited the tunnel before the Dykeman Street stop. This is because the No. 1 train travels along a trussel for that portion of its run. One day, as I was looking out the door windows, when the train was coming into the 207th Street station, I happened to see a group of men who were chasing one man on the street below. The man who was being chased was easily outrunning the group of men who were chasing him. But instead of looking where he was going, he kept looking back at the men who were chasing him. As a result, he ran straight into a light pole when he looked back at the men who were chasing him. Because he looked back, his neck became a hook that got caught onto the light pole, causing him to be flung around it almost 360 degrees. As well, when he was flung around the light pole, his feet were completely up in the air because he was running so fast. This resulted in him being slim violently onto the ground when he flew off of the light pole. The last sight that I saw as a train entered the station was the men surrounding him as he sat, dazed and confused on the ground. My brothers, I said all of this to say that in the same manner, if we as men fail to keep looking forward on our pathway to freedom, we could wind up being flung around an obstacle only to find ourselves sitting on the ground, dazed and confused. For we free men, it is to looking back at the negative aspects of our lives, with somehow chase us in a haunting manner. It is also the component of things which are done to us on a day-to-day basis, like the constant shaming of who we are as free men. AKA, you will be nothing without a woman and you will die alone because you choose to be free. My brothers, rather than to allow conditions in our lives which can create days and confused states which fully inhibit our freedom, we must all keep our eyes open and fully focus on our pathway to freedom. As well, we must be vigilant and doing therefore mention both individually and corporately as free men. Finally, my brothers, it is where you are headed towards, the incomprehensible nature of your freedom, which is fully inclusive of fully understanding the vast powers and capabilities we all possess as free men. As you step forward into 2024 and beyond my brothers, never, ever stop looking forward. This is the Mektaw infinium and this has been an infinium short take. My Mektaw brothers as always, stay safe, stay strong, stay on the Mektaw path and remember, Mektaw is the liberation of men's minds. Mektaw cannot and will not be stopped.

Transcript: Brothers and sisters, we gather here today to celebrate the Lord's favor. His blessings are abundant. His love knows no bounds. Let us open our hearts to His grace and receive His blessings. Let us pray. Father, we come before you today with open hearts and minds. We seek your guidance and your grace. Pour your spirit upon us. Fill us with your love and your power. In Jesus' name, we pray, amen. In Luke 4 verses 18 and 19, we hear the words of Isaiah fulfilled in Jesus. These verses are a powerful declaration of His mission and purpose on earth. The Spirit of the Lord is on me because He has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. This proclamation is not just a statement but a promise of hope and transformation for those who are marginalized and suffering. He has sent me to proclaim freedom for the prisoners. This freedom is not only physical but also spiritual. This is a sign of liberation from the chains of sin and despair and recovery of sight for the blind. This signifies not only the miraculous healing of physical blindness but also the opening of our spiritual eyes to see the truth and light of God's love, to set the oppressed free. Jesus came to break the bonds of oppression whether they are social, economic or spiritual and to bring justice and peace to those who are downtrodden, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor. This is a time of Jubilee, a season of grace and mercy where debts are forgiven and lives are restored. Jesus, anointed by the Holy Spirit, was empowered to bring healing and hope. His ministry was marked by miracles and acts of compassion showing us the heart of God. He was sent to deliver the good news. This good news is the gospel of salvation, offering eternal life to all who believe in Him. He was chosen to set the captives free. This freedom extends to all areas of life, breaking the chains of addiction, fear and hopelessness. This same spirit lives within each of us today. As believers, we are filled with the Holy Spirit who empowers us to continue the work of Jesus. We too are called to be vessels of His love. Our mission is to share His love and grace with those around us, bringing light to the darkness. We are empowered to make a difference in the world. Through acts of kindness, service and compassion, we can reflect the love of Christ and bring about positive change in our communities. Just as Jesus was anointed and empowered, we too are given the strength and courage to face the challenges of our time. We are called to be His hands and feet, reaching out to those in need. Our actions, no matter how small, can have a profound impact. When we serve others, we are serving Christ Himself. And our efforts are multiplied by His grace. Let us embrace our calling with joy and dedication, knowing that we are part of a greater purpose. Together we can bring hope and healing to a broken world. As we go forth, let us remember the words of Jesus and the mission He has entrusted to us. With the Holy Spirit as our guide, we can accomplish great things for His glory. May we always be mindful of the anointing we have received and the empowerment that comes from the Holy Spirit. Let us walk in faith, love and service, bringing the good news to all corners of the earth. Lord, we thank You for the power of Your Holy Spirit. Give us the boldness to walk in Your anointing. Help us to be Your hands and feet. Use us to bring healing and hope to those in need. We pray this in Jesus' name, amen. In Luke 9, Jesus gives His disciples a powerful mission. He gathers them together, imparting wisdom and strength, preparing them for the journey ahead. This moment is pivotal as it marks the beginning of their active ministry. He sends them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal the sick. This mission is not just about words, but about actions that demonstrate the power and love of God. The disciples are to be living examples of the message they carry. He gives them authority over demons and the power to perform miracles. This authority is a testament to their divine calling, enabling them to confront the forces of darkness and bring light to those in need. Your mission is both spiritual and practical, addressing the physical and spiritual needs of the people. This same mission extends to us today. We are not just passive recipients of this message, but active participants in its propagation. The call to serve, to heal, and to spread the good news is as relevant now as it was then. Transcript: Thailand grants citizenship to 483,000 migrants. The Thai government's recent decision to grant citizenship to a significant number of migrants in ethnic minorities has received a warm welcome from the National Human Rights Commission, and HRC. The move, announced by the Cabinet yesterday, aims to provide Thai citizenship to over 483,000 individuals who have either been residing in Thailand for an extended period, or were born within the country. This policy, proposed by the National Security Council, seeks to streamline the process of granting legal status to ethnic minorities. The revised framework allows applicants to self-certify their qualifications and criminal history, removing the need for protracted investigations by various agencies. Wastant Paylee-Clie, a commissioner with the NHRFC, highlighted the significance of this government action as it reaffirms Thailand's dedication to the pledges made during the high-level segment on statelessness in 2019. This event, held in Geneva, saw Thailand and Orsa campaign aiming to eradicate statelessness by the year 2024. Prime Minister Pete Hong-Tarrenshin-A-Wat mentioned that there are currently 825,635 individuals in Thailand awaiting confirmation of their status, with 483,626 of them lined up to benefit from this new policy. This development aligns with international human rights principles, the Thai Constitution, and the international covenant on civil and political rights, Iqfur, which Thailand has ratified, said the Thai PM. The Cabinet resolution is in line with international human rights principles and the country's commitment to human rights. While the NHRFC uploads this step towards addressing statelessness, Wastant also emphasized the importance of safeguarding the process from abuse and corruption. He urged the government to ensure the policy achieves its goal of promoting equality. It's crucial that this policy does not become a tool for corruption, and that it serves its intended purpose. The NHRFC has been actively involved in addressing the challenges of statelessness, collaborating with relevant agencies to offer solutions. Last year, the Commission presented guidelines at a seminar to enhance access to basic rights and welfare for stateless individuals. This initiative marks a significant stride in addressing the longstanding issue of statelessness in Thailand, reflecting a commitment to human rights and equality. The NHRC's endorsement underscores the importance of integrity and transparency in implementing such policies, reported BankUp Post.

Transcript: Good morning folks, we'll be taking a look at some solar activity, we'll peek in on two new missions to study the sun, and we'll see about a 2024 science event that I am hoping at least one observer can attend. But we are starting, as always, with the last 24 hours on our star, and we find several eruptive events, a couple more small M-class flares, and several more plasma filaments and sunspots turning across the Earth-facing heliographic longitudes. While there's nothing major heading our way, a plasma filament eruption has caught my eye here this morning. It occurred overnight at the incoming Northern filament, and was just one of several eruptions that happened overnight. None are massive, or poised to deliver major impacts to Earth, but amidst those eruptions, the filament may be heading our way, we will have both eyes on the sun and on the solar wind in the days ahead. First up in the mission log is punch, a fleet of small satellites is going to map the solar wind from its departure from the sun, through the inner heliosphere and should be telling us about the evolution of both normal ambient streams and coronal mass ejections. The other mission is sunrise, a suite of six satellites whose job will be to monitor and study those explosive events, the solar flares and CMEs, should be some excellent science from these two missions coming over the next several years. Last but not least, they are going to hold the 10 year anniversary meeting of the swarm mission in Denmark in April of 2024. This will be the perfect opportunity to either get the information we have sought or ask a question to probe on the topic. If they're ever going to update the strength figures of the Earth's magnetic field, it'll be done here. If not, you'll surely get the opportunity to ask about it. Any observer who plans on going, please let me know. Transcript: Hi everyone, it's Ms. Dragonfly, the relationship whisperer back again. And today's topic is, should you both have even say in everything? What we are constantly being told through the media and modern societies, that couples should have equal say in everything to be fair, keep both happy and also for equality's sake. Now common thinking and advice from all experts is we need to make decisions together as then both will have their inputs and therefore should agree and be happy with the decision made. This also will support equality in marriage. Oh wait, hold on, is this correct? Well, most relationship advice given is to please have equal say in everything, which is wrong. Basically to have equal say in everything is like making decisions as a committee which means it takes longer to reach a decision and will not produce the best decision possible. So why is that? Well, everyone has different skills and are good at different things. Therefore to have equal say for everyone in everything does not make sense as the decision made then is not going to produce an optimum outcome. Take for example, when you're building a house, you have the carpenter and the plumber who are good at what they do and have different skill sets. Of course, now should both the carpenter and the plumber discuss and agree on every part of the job? Should the carpenter also agree with the plumber to have equal say as to how the toilet and drainage pipes are to be installed? On the other hand, should the plumber then also have equal say as to how the house frame is going to be put up? Now you know that they themselves are going to know that they have different skills so it will then like no sense for them both to have equal say in each other's speciality. How it usually works is they both trust each other to do their jobs according to their skills and their area of expertise. Of course. Now this should be the same in relationships and marriage. Each person has their own different skill sets, set of skills, so the partners should be trusting each other to do their jobs that they're going to be good at or they are good at. But at the same time keep each other up to date as to what they're doing and why. For example, should the partner with no financial skills and a bad financial record have equal say in managing the money? They should have no say in it if you want to have the right decisions being made. They can have a say in what their financial goals as a couple. You know for the importance of mutual goals. However, knowing their lack of skills in this matter, this area, the partner with a better skills should be the one allowed to solely manage the finances. A case in point is Carol and Graham. Carol has always been a borrower and never saved anything but insisted on having her say in everything and decisions had to go her way. Graham worked his way up the corporate ladder and became an executive on an executive salary. Will not surprisingly after 30 years of marriage they ended up having to live on the pension as they had to spend all their money on holidays and luxuries. Even any property they owned was sold off to fund the lifestyle that Carol had grown accustomed to. Graham had to go along with her wishes as there would have been arguments and screaming from her even though he knew better. They were always under constant financial stress. Partners should definitely not have equal say in all decisions. Personal pride and once should not get in the way of deciding who is in charge of what, which should be according to each person's personal skill set. As only that way you're going to have the best decisions being made without being compromised by the unskilled partner in this and achieve the optimum outcomes. By stepping back and allowing your partner to make decisions that they are good at, it's also a matter of trust. That you trust your partner to make the right choices and trust is what is definitely needed if you want your marriage to last. So those are my thoughts on the matter, what do you think? Let me know if I leave in your comments below and if you've enjoyed the video then don't forget to like, share and subscribe. And for more info on relationships, check out this video. And that's it for this segment and until I see you next, remember to stay safe, confident and gorgeous.

Transcript: In John 14, Jesus says, I am the way the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me. There are few beliefs that offend and even confuse our postmodern, post-Christian culture. Like this claim, the Bible unapologetically says that there is salvation by grace alone, through faith alone in Jesus Christ. This is a truth claim, but not just a truth claim. It's an exclusive truth claim. The claim that our culture would rather us believe, the claim that our culture is more comfortable with, is that there are many ways, there are many truths, and there are many lives, and no one can tell you which one is better than the other. Think about this quote from a German physicist named Max Born. He says, the belief that there is only one truth and that one self is in possession of it is the root of all evil in the world. It's a really bold claim. So what do we do with that? Is it arrogant for us as Christians to believe that we are right and other people are wrong? Is it evil for us to believe? So how are we to respond to this subjection? First, let's consider what the quote from this German physicist. What he's saying is, he says that to claim that you have truth and that others don't have it is the root of all evil in the world. The problem with that claim is that he does what he's saying you can't do. In other words, he's making an exclusive truth claim stating that you can't make exclusive truth claims. So it's hypocritical. It's contradictory. And this is the problem with the idea of inclusivism. To truly be inclusive, you would have to be inclusive of beliefs and systems that make exclusive claims. If you're not truly inclusive of those, then you yourself become exclusive. The point is this, that you cannot make a truth claim. You cannot say that something is true without, at the same time, saying that other things are not true, it's simply impossible to do. So think about this. If somebody were to tell you, just like what this guy says in his quote, if somebody was to tell you that you can't tell people how to live their lives, they've just done to you what they're telling you that you can't do to other people.
